rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse commands completing Hajj and Umrah once one undertakes them for God; it does not establish that initiating either rite is obligatory.
rows.anchor: أي أجعلوهما تامين إذا تصديتم لأدائهما لوجه الله تعالى فلا دلالة في الآية على أكثر من وجوب الإتمام بعد الشروع فيهما

rows.speaker: الحنفية والشافعية
rows.claim: Both schools agree that spoiling Hajj or Umrah requires continuing the remaining rites and making them up.
rows.anchor: فإن إفساد الحج والعمرة مطلقا يوجب المضي في بقية الأفعال والقضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rule that whatever is needed to fulfill an unrestricted obligation is obligatory does not prove an initial duty here, because completion presupposes that one has begun.
rows.anchor: لأن الأمر بالإتمام يقتضي سابقية الشروع فيكون الأمر بالإتمام مقيدا بالشروع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading the command as “perform the rites in a complete state,” with the variant “وأقيموا,” departs from the apparent sense and may make completeness, rather than performance, the commanded duty.
rows.anchor: وإدعاء أن المعنى أئتوا بهما حال كونهما تامين مستجمعي الشرائط والأركان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command in Ibn Masud’s variant can mean a request that covers both obligatory and recommended acts; reports favoring recommendation provide its contextual cue.
rows.anchor: الأمر في القراءة محمول على المعنى المجازي المشترك بين الواجب والمندوب

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report transmitted by al-Shafi‘i and others describes Hajj as jihad and Umrah as voluntary.
rows.anchor: أنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال : الحج جهاد والعمرة تطوع

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In a report from Jabir authenticated by al-Tirmidhi, the Prophet says Umrah is not obligatory, though performing it is better.
rows.anchor: وصححهعن جابرأن رجلا سأل رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن العمرة أواجبة هي

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says Hajj is obligatory while Umrah is voluntary.
rows.anchor: إبن مسعود صاحب هذه القراءة قال فيما أخرجه عنه إبن أبي شيبة وعبد بن حميد : الحج فريضة والعمرة تطوع

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reportedly recited “وأقيموا الحج والعمرة” but said he would call Umrah obligatory only if he had heard the Prophet say so.
rows.anchor: أنه كان يقرأ ذلك ثم يقول : والله لولا التحرج أني لم أسمع فيها من رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم شيئا لقلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Masud’s hesitation suggests that he did not understand his variant command as making Umrah obligatory, since he lacked a Prophetic report to that effect.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أنه رضي الله تعالى عنه لم يجعل الأمر بالنسبة إليها للوجوب لأنه لم يسمع شيئا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports of recommendation can qualify the command only if they predate the verse; otherwise that reading would abrogate the Quran by a solitary report.
rows.anchor: نعم لا يعد ما ذكر صارفا إلا إذا ثبت كونه قبل الآية أما إذا ثبت كونه بعدها فلا لأنه يلزم نسخ الكتاب بخبر الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that earlier recommendation reports abrogate the command reverses the evidentiary hierarchy: a Quranic apparent meaning cannot abrogate a hadith explicit in recommendation.
rows.anchor: لأن الأحاديث نص في الإستحباب والقرآن ظاهر في الوجوب فكيف يكون الظاهر ناسخا للنص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These arguments do not erase the supporting force of the recommendation reports, but they substantially weaken it.
rows.anchor: وإن لم يكن مبطلا لأصل التأييد إلا أنه يضعفه جدا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some argue that reports making Umrah recommended are opposed by reports that make it obligatory.
rows.anchor: وأدعى بعضهم أن الأحاديث الدالة على إستحباب العمرة معارضة بما يدل على وجوبها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Hakim transmits from Zayd ibn Thabit a Prophetic report calling Hajj and Umrah two obligations and allowing either to be begun first.
rows.anchor: قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم : إن الحج والعمرة فريضتان

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: A man told Umar that he found Hajj and Umrah prescribed and had entered ihram for both; Umar said he had followed the Prophet’s practice.
rows.anchor: أن رجلا قال لعمر : إني وجدت الحج والعمرة مكتوبين علي أهللت بهما جميعا فقال : هديت لسنة نبيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umar’s response supports the view that entering ihram for both together was a Prophetic practice, since a Companion’s report of that practice conveys an actual Prophetic precedent.
rows.anchor: فإن هذا يدل على أن الإهلال بهما طريقة النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم لأن الإستدلال بما حكاه الصحابي من سننه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The suggestion that the man’s “I entered ihram” explains how he found both obligatory fails: the two clauses form a question and answer, so finding them prescribed caused his ihram.
rows.anchor: لأن الجملة مستأنفة كأنه قيل : فما فعلت فقال : أهللت فيدل على ان الوجدان سبب الإهلال دون العكس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umar’s answer does not address an obligation to complete rites after starting; that is not called the Prophet’s practice, whereas performing the rites and acts of worship is.
rows.anchor: وجواب عمر رضي الله تعالى عنه بمعزل عن وجوب الإتمام لأن كون الشروع في الشيء موجبا لإتمامه لا يقال فيه أنه طريقة النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reading with fa, “فأهللت,” strengthens the sequence in which finding the rites prescribed precedes entering ihram.
rows.anchor: الروايات فأهللتبالفاء الدالة على الترتب

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud’s position that Umrah is obligatory is countered by another report from him; Ali also held obligation and recited “وأقيموا,” as did Ibn Abbas and Ibn Umar.
rows.anchor: وما ذكر عن إبن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه معارض بما روى عنه من القول بالوجوب وبذلك قال علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports conflict, and each imam followed the reports he regarded as sound; the disagreement concerns a subsidiary legal issue and is a mercy.
rows.anchor: والإنصاف تسليم تعارض الأخابر وقد أخذ كل من الأئمة بما صح عنده والمسألة من الفروع والإختلاف في أمثالها رحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is not evidence for the Shafiis and those agreeing with them that Hajj and Umrah are initially obligatory; it requires completion after undertaking them and guidance for impediments.
rows.anchor: الآية لا تصلح دليلا للشافعية ومن وافقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The obligation of Hajj is instead established by the command that people perform pilgrimage to the House if able.
rows.anchor: ( ولله على الناس حج البيت من إستطاع إليه سبيلا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opponents who claim this verse proves their position have, in the author’s judgment, made a serious interpretive error.
rows.anchor: ومن أدعى من المخالفين أنه دليل له فقد ركب شططا وقال غلطا

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali explains completing Hajj and Umrah as entering ihram for them from one’s own home; a similar report is raised from Abu Hurayra to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أخرج إبن جرير وإبن المنذر والبيهقي وجماعة عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه إتمام الحج والعسرة لله أن تحرم بهما من دويرة أهلك

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar says completion includes performing each rite separately and performing Umrah outside the months of Hajj.
rows.anchor: عن إبن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنهما من إتمامهما أن يفرد كل واحد منهما عن الآخر وأن يعتمر في غير أشهر الحج

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other reported interpretations of completing the rites require lawful spending, a separate journey for each, or setting out solely to perform them rather than for trade.
rows.anchor: إتمامهما أن تكون النفقة حلالا وقيل : أن تحدث لكل منهما سفرا وقيل : أن تخرج قاصدا لهما لا لتجارة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: A variant reads “إلى البيت,” transmitted from Ibn Masud.
rows.anchor: والأول مروى عن إبن مسعود والثاني عن علي

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A variant reads “للبيت,” transmitted from Ali.
rows.anchor: والثاني عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “If you are prevented” presupposes an omitted condition: the preceding instruction applies when you are able to complete the rites.
rows.anchor: فإن أحصرتم مقابل لمحذوف أي هذا إن قدرتم على إتمامهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In their original lexical sense, both ḥaṣr and iḥṣār mean obstruction generally, rather than being divided between enemy and illness.
rows.anchor: والإحصار والحصر كلاهما في أصل اللغة بمعنى المنع مطلقا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj assigns ḥaṣr to obstruction by enemies and iḥṣār to obstruction through illness or fear, based on common usage.
rows.anchor: والإحصار بما يكون من المرض والخوفكما توهم الزجاجمن كثرة إستعمالهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Common use of a general word for one case does not make that case part of its lexical meaning; forms used with enemies also undermine the proposed distinction.
rows.anchor: والدليل على ذلك أنه يقال : حصره العدو وأحصره كصده وأصده

rows.speaker: مالك والشافعي
rows.claim: Malik and al-Shafii restrict the verse’s iḥṣār to enemy obstruction, citing the contrast with safety, the Hudaybiyya setting, and Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: والمراد من الإحصار هنا حصر العدو عند مالك والشافعي رحمهما الله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says there is no iḥṣār except obstruction by an enemy; the author says this restricts the verse’s unrestricted wording.
rows.anchor: ولقول إبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما لا حصر إلا حصر العدو فقيد إطلاق الآية

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa reads iḥṣār broadly to cover any impediment, including enemies, illness, and other causes.
rows.anchor: وذهب الإمام أبو حنيفة إلى أن المراد به ما يعم كل منع من عدو ومرض وغيرهما

rows.speaker: الحجاج بن عمرو
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says that a pilgrim who is broken or lamed must perform Hajj again the following year.
rows.anchor: من حديث الحجاج بن عمرو من كسر أو عرج فعليه الحج من قابل

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: When a man in ihram for Umrah was stung and incapacitated, Ibn Masud advised sending a sacrifice, marking a day, and releasing him once slaughter was likely.
rows.anchor: فقال : أبعثوا بالهدى وأجعلوا بينكم وبينه يوم أمارة فإذا كان ذلك فليحل

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata says iḥṣār can result from illness, an enemy, or any obstructing event; Bukhari transmits a similar report.
rows.anchor: وأخرج إبن أبي شيبة عن عطاء لا إحصار إلا من مرض أو عدو أو أمر حابس وروى البخاري مثله عنه

rows.speaker: عروة
rows.claim: Urwa says anything that detains a pilgrim in ihram counts as iḥṣār.
rows.anchor: وقال عروة : كل شيء حبس المحرم فهو إحصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The specific occasion does not restrict the rule; reading the verse merely as confirmation conflicts with its independent lām construction.
rows.anchor: وأما الثاني فإنه لا عبرة بخصوص السبب والحمل على أنه للتأييد يأبى عنه ذكره باللام استقلالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the past-tense verb is not general, it is unrestricted and therefore can include impediments beyond the enemy detention in the reported occasion.
rows.anchor: والقول بأن أحصرتمليس عاما إذ الفعل المثبت لا عموم له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas’s restrictive report is opposed by his broader explanation that either debilitating illness or an enemy can prevent a pilgrim from reaching the House.
rows.anchor: معارض بما أخرجه إبن جرير وإبن المنذر عنه في تفسير الآية أنه كان يقول من أحرم بحج أو عمرة ثم حبس عن البيت بمرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the Hajjaj report weak is itself weak: it has several routes, and Ikrima reports that Abbas and Abu Hurayra affirmed it.
rows.anchor: إذ له طرق مختلفة في السنن وقد روى أبو داؤد

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima asked Abbas and Abu Hurayra about the report, and both said it was true.
rows.anchor: وقد روى أبو داؤد أن عكرمة سأل العباس وأبا هريرة رضي الله تعالى عنهما عن ذلك فقالا : صدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Restricting the rule to a pilgrim who stipulates release upon an impediment does not fit Hanafi legal theory, which preserves an unrestricted text unless the relevant cases and rulings align.
rows.anchor: لا يتمشى على ما تقرر في أصول الحنفية من أن المطلق يجري على إطلاقه إلا إذا أتحد الحادثة والحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “What is readily available of the sacrifice” means that a sacrifice is due, using an omitted obligation or command; “استيسر” means became available, not sought after.
rows.anchor: أي فعليكم أو فالواجب أو فأهدوا ما أستيسر أي تيسر فهو كصعب وأستصعب وليست السين للطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hady is a verbal noun used as a passive noun for the animal offered, and can refer to one animal or several; another reading doubles the yāʾ as a plural of hadiyya.
rows.anchor: مصدر بمعنى المفعول أي المهدي ولذلك يطلق على الفرد والجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “هدي” in the doubled reading is grammatically a circumstantial qualifier of the implicit subject in “استيسر.”
rows.anchor: وقريء هدي بالتشديد جمع هدية كمطي ومطية وهو في موضع الحال من الضمير المستكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prevented pilgrim seeking release slaughters whichever camel, cow, or sheep is available.
rows.anchor: أن المحرم إذا أحصر وأراد أن يتحلل تحلل بذبح هدي تيسر عليه من بدنة أو بقرة أو شاة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says a larger sacrificial animal is better.
rows.anchor: قال إبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنه : وما عظم فهو أفضل

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar limits the sacrifice to a cow or camel and says a sheep does not suffice.
rows.anchor: وعن إبن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه خص الهدى ببقرة أو جزور فقيل له : أو ما يكفيه شاة فقال : لا

rows.speaker: مالك والشافعي
rows.claim: Most scholars say the sacrifice is made where the pilgrim was prevented, relying on the Prophet’s sacrifice at Hudaybiyya.
rows.anchor: ويذبحه حيث أحصر عند الأكثر لأنه صلى الله عليه وسلم ذبح عام الحديبية بها

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: The Hanafi position sends the sacrifice to the sanctuary and releases the pilgrim after the appointed marker day when slaughter is likely.
rows.anchor: وعندنا يبعث من أحصر به ويجعل للمبعوث بيده يوم أمارة فإذا جاء اليوم وغلب على ظنه أنه ذبح تحلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shaving is a metonym for leaving ihram, including a woman’s shortening of hair; the nearest addressee is the prevented pilgrim.
rows.anchor: فإن حلق الرأس كناية عن الحل الذي يحصل بالتقصير بالنسبة للنساء والخطاب للمحصرين لأنه أقرب مذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second mention of the sacrifice refers to the first; the Hanafi reading requires waiting until the animal sent to the sanctuary reaches its prescribed place of slaughter.
rows.anchor: والهدي الثاني عين الأول كما هو الظاهر أي لا تحلوا حتى تعلموا أن الهدي المبعوث إلى الحرم بلغ مكانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author links the appointed place to the House and the Kaaba through two other Quranic formulations.
rows.anchor: ( ثم محلها إلى البيت العتيق ) ( هديا بالغ الكعبة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s sacrifice at Hudaybiyya is established, but the claim that he slaughtered outside the sanctuary is not; Hanafis locate it in the adjoining Haram area.
rows.anchor: وما روى من ذبحه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم في الحديبية مسلم لكن كونه ذبح في الحل غير مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hanafi account reconciles Malik’s report with Zuhri’s report that the Prophet slaughtered in the Haram, while questioning whether the latter narration is established.
rows.anchor: وبه يجمع بين ما قاله مالك وبين ما روى الزهري أن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم نحر في الحرم

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: The earlier scholars take the appointed place to mean any place where slaughter is valid, inside or outside the Haram; this departs from the apparent wording but avoids adding “know.”
rows.anchor: وحمل الأولون بلوغ الهدي محله على ذبحه حيث يحل ذبحه فيه حلا كان أو حرما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inference that the verse’s mention of sacrifice excludes a make-up obligation fails: the Prophet and Companions made up the Hudaybiyya Umrah, called the Umrah of compensation.
rows.anchor: وعندنا يجب القضاء لقضاء رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وأصحابه عمرة الحديبية التي أحصروا فيها وكانت تسمى عمرة القضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage explains how a prevented pilgrim exits ihram, not every duty; the rule for other pilgrims follows by implication, while coordinating the shaving ban with the opening command disrupts the sequence.
rows.anchor: والمقام مقام بيان طريق خروج المحصر عن الإحرام لا مقام بيان كل ما يجب عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With kasra, “maḥill” can mean a place, which is most apparent here, or a time, as in the due date of a debt.
rows.anchor: المحلبالكسر من حد ضرب يطلق للمكان كما هو الظاهر في الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Illness or harm to the head qualifies the ban on shaving; the harm includes wounds, lice, and headache, and the atonement applies if the pilgrim shaves.
rows.anchor: يحتاج للحلق وهو مخصص لقوله سبحانه ( ولا تحلقوا ) متفرع عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “From fasting, charity, or sacrifice” identifies the kinds of atonement, not their amounts.
rows.anchor: بيان الجنس الفدية وأما قدرها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet told Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra at Hudaybiyya to shave and choose among feeding six poor people a farq of food, fasting three days, or offering a sacrifice.
rows.anchor: عن كعب ابن عجرة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ' مر به وهو بالحديبية

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A second version says that, when Kaʿb lacked a sheep, he should fast three days or feed six people half a ṣāʿ each, then shave.
rows.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال له : ما كنت أرى أن الجهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second report specifies the amount for each poor person but not where the atonement must be paid.
rows.anchor: وقد بين في هذه الرواية ما يطعم لكل مسكين ولم يبين محل الفدية

rows.speaker: ابن الفرس
rows.claim: Ibn al-Faras holds that the atonement is unrestricted as to location; this is also Malik’s position.
rows.anchor: كما قاله ابن الفرس ، وهو مذهب الأماممالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “When you are safe” can mean being in security and ease, or the removal of the fear of obstruction.
rows.anchor: أو الأمنة زواله فعلى الأول معناه فإذا كنتم في أمن وسعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase also implies the ruling for someone who was safe from the outset, and its fa coordinates this clause with the earlier prevention clause.
rows.anchor: ويفهم منه حكم من كان آمنا ابتداءا بطريق الدلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa indicates sequence whether prevention means enemy detention or any kind of impediment.
rows.anchor: مفيدة للتعقيب سواء أريد حصر العدو أو كل منع في الوجود

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibrahim transmits that “safe” can describe a sick person whose illness has passed; the author says this weakens the enemy-only reading of al-Shafii and Malik.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود . وابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهم من طريق إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa answers “when you are safe”; the bāʾ and ilāʾ attach to tamattuʿ, meaning to benefit from drawing near to God through Umrah before the Hajj season.
rows.anchor: فمن استمتع وانتفع بالتقريب إلى الله تعال بالعمرة إلى وقت الحج

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative makes the bāʾ causal and leaves the object of enjoyment unstated: Umrah allows release from ihram restrictions until Hajj, using the word in its ordinary rather than technical sense.
rows.anchor: ومتعلق التمتع محذوف أي بشيء من محذورات الاحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In its technical sense, tamattuʿ is performing Umrah in the Hajj months, completing it, and then entering ihram for Hajj from within Mecca.
rows.anchor: والأول هو أن يحرم بالعمرة في أشهر الحج ويأتي بمناسكها ثم يحرم بالحج من جوف مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qirān means entering ihram for Hajj and Umrah together, with the Hajj rites encompassing the Umrah rites.
rows.anchor: ويقابله القران وهو يحرم بهما معا ويأتي بمناسك الحج فيدخل فيما مناسك العمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ifrād means entering ihram for Hajj and performing Umrah after completing Hajj.
rows.anchor: والافراد وهو أن يحرم بالحج وبعد الفراغ منه بالعمرة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafii treats the tamattuʿ sacrifice as compensatory: the pilgrim should have entered ihram for Hajj at the miqat, so the sacrifice repairs that defect; it is not due from Meccans.
rows.anchor: فهو دم جبران لأن الواجب عليه أن يحرم للحج من الميقات فلما أحرم لا من المقيات أورث ذلك خللا فيه

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: On al-Shafii’s view, the sacrifice is due when the pilgrim enters ihram for Hajj, may be offered before the Day of Sacrifice though that day is preferred, and should not be eaten.
rows.anchor: ويذبحه إذا أحرم بالحج ولا يجوز قبل الاحرام ولا يتعين له يوم النحر بل يستحب ولا يأكل منه

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa regards the sacrifice as a ritual offering, like that of a qārin, owed in gratitude for combining the two rites and slaughtered on the Day of Sacrifice.
rows.anchor: وذهب الإمام أبو حنيفة إلى أنه دم نسك كدم القارن لأنه وجب عليه شكرا للجمع بين النسكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about those who cannot find a sacrifice is coordinated with “when you are safe.”
rows.anchor: وهو عطف على ( فإذا امنتم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading “فصيام” with accusative can be read as an imperative, “so let him fast”; the time adjunct for fasting is omitted because no Hajj act can itself be its time.
rows.anchor: وظرف الصوم محذوف إذ يمتنع أن يكون شيء من أعمال الحج ظرفا له

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa reads “during Hajj” broadly as the Hajj period between the two ihrams, covering fasting before Hajj ihram whether or not Umrah has been completed, as well as fasting afterward.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو حنيفة : المراد في وقت الحج مطلقا لكن بين الإحرامين إحرام الحج وإحرام العمرة

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: If the pilgrim obtains a sacrifice after three fasts but before leaving ihram, Abu Hanifa requires slaughter; after release, the fast has achieved its purpose and slaughter is no longer due.
rows.anchor: بدليل أنه إذا قدر على الهدى بعد صوم الثلاثة قبل التحلل وجب عليه الذبح ولو قدر عليه بعد التحلل لا يجب عليه

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafii confines the fast to the period of performing Hajj after ihram and before release; it cannot precede Hajj ihram.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي : المراد وقت أداء الحج وهو أيام الاشتغال به بعد الإحرام وقبل التحلل ولا يجوز الصوم عنده قبل إحرام الحج

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafii prefers fasting on the seventh, eighth, and ninth of Dhul-Hijja, and bars fasting on the Day of Sacrifice and the Tashriq days.
rows.anchor: والأحب أن يصوم سابع ذي الحجة وثامنه وتاسعه لأنه غاية ما يمكن في التأخير

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some scholars permit fasting the final three days of Tashriq, citing Ibn Umar’s report that the Prophet allowed a tamattu pilgrim who had not fasted during the first ten days to fast them instead.
rows.anchor: رخص النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم للتمتع إذا لم يجد الهدي

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Zuhri reports that the Prophet sent Abdullah ibn Hudhafa to announce that the Tashriq days are for eating, drinking, and remembering God, except for someone fasting in place of a sacrifice.
rows.anchor: بعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عبدالله بن حذافة فنادى في أيام التشريق

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Al-Daraqutni transmits a similar report through Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib.
rows.anchor: وأخرج الدارقطني مثله من طريق سعيد بن المسيب

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet allowed fasting during the Tashriq days only for a tamattu pilgrim who lacked a sacrifice; Malik adopted this view.
rows.anchor: قالت : لم يرخص صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم في أيام التشريق أن يضمن

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: The Hanafis rely on reports prohibiting fasting on those days: if the three-day fast is missed until the Day of Sacrifice, only the original sacrifice suffices, and the fast is not made up afterward.
rows.anchor: وقالوا : إذا فاته الصوم حتى أتى يوم النحر لم يجزه إلا الدم

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar ordered a sheep to be slaughtered in a comparable case.
rows.anchor: وعن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه أمر في مثله بذبح الشاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “When you return” can mean finishing and departing from the rites, or returning from Mina; al-Shafii’s school generally prefers return to one’s family.
rows.anchor: أي فرغتم ونفرتم من أعماله فذكر الرجوع وأريد سببه أو المعنى إذا رجعتم من منى

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafii’s more widely accepted view takes return to mean returning to one’s family, supported by Ibn Abbas and the word’s more apparent sense.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنهعلى ما هو الأصح عند معظم أصحابه : إذا رجعتم إلى أهليكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas’s report glosses the return as reaching one’s home towns.
rows.anchor: عن إبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنه إذا رجعتم إلى أمصاركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Someone intending permanent residence in Mecca is treated like one returning to their homeland, since the law treats a place of residence as a home.
rows.anchor: وحكم ناوي الإقامة بمكة توطنا حكم الراجع إلى وطنه لأن الشرع أقام موضع الإقامة مقام الوطن

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Al-Bahr records two interpretations of returning to one’s family: beginning the journey home or reaching home.
rows.anchor: وفي البحر المراد بالرجوع إلى الأهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading “سبعة” in the accusative coordinates with the grammatical position of “ثلاثة أيام”; those who reject this analysis supply an implied “fast.”
rows.anchor: بالنصب عطفا على محل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those ten complete” refers to the three and seven days together, with “days” omitted; the feminine form is the more common usage when the counted noun is omitted.
rows.anchor: الإشارة إلى الثلاثة والسبعة ومميز العدد محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The summation prevents readers from taking the conjunction as an alternative, and al-Sirafi notes that waw can convey that sense of clarification.
rows.anchor: وقد نص السيرافي في شرح الكتاب على مجيئها لذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A preceding explicit command is not required: a declarative statement with imperative force can also serve the same purpose.
rows.anchor: وليس تقدم الأمر الصريح شرطا فيه بل الخبر الذي هو بمعنى الأمر كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording removes a remote misunderstanding and reinforces knowledge of the total both as a whole and as separate parts.
rows.anchor: وأن يعلم العدد جملة كما علم تفصيلافيحاط به من وجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repetition suits a broad audience, reinforces understanding, and makes clear that seven is an exact number rather than a large indefinite quantity.
rows.anchor: بتكرار الكلام وزيادة الإفهام والإيذان بأن المراد بالسبعة العدد دون الكثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because fasting replaces the sacrifice, three days fall during Hajj and seven afterward to balance its value without reducing reward; placing all seven during Hajj would impose hardship.
rows.anchor: والبدل يكون في محل المبدل منه غالبا جعل الثلاثة بدلا عنه في زمن الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description “complete” signals that the ten balance the sacrifice without loss of reward.
rows.anchor: وصفت العشرة بأنها ( كاملة ) فكأنه قيل : ( تلك عشرة كاملة )

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view treats “complete” as emphasis and an added recommendation to perform all ten fasts without neglect or reduction.
rows.anchor: تفيد زيادة التوصية بصيامها وأن لا يتهاون بها ولا ينقص من عددها

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: A further interpretation calls ten a complete number because it ends the count and the numbers after it combine ten with what precedes.
rows.anchor: صفة مبينة كمال العشرة فإنها عدد كمل فيه خواص الأعداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Imam offers ten explanations for the summation and its description, but the author calls them incomplete and omits them to avoid excessive length.
rows.anchor: وذكر الإمام لهذه الفذلكة مع الوصف عشرة أوجهلكنها عشرة غير كاملة

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa takes “that” to refer to tamattuʿ: residents of the sanctuary have no tamattuʿ or qirān because avoiding one of two journeys is no benefit to Meccans.
rows.anchor: عند أبي حنيفة رضي الله تعالى عنه إذ لا متعة ولا قرآن لحاضري المسجد

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafii takes “that” to refer to the obligation of sacrifice or its replacement for a nonresident tamattu pilgrim, whose Hajj ihram from within Mecca departs from the miqat.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه : إنها إشارة إلى الأقرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author objects that if “that” referred to the sacrifice and fast, the text should say “على” rather than “لمن”; reading the lām as “upon” is against the apparent usage.
rows.anchor: لأتيبعليدون اللام في قوله سبحانه : لمن لم يكن أهله حاضري المسجد الحرام

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafii defines those present at the sanctuary as people within the distance of a travel allowance.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالموصول من كان من الحرم على مسافة القصر عند الشافعي

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa defines them as people whose homes are beyond the miqat.
rows.anchor: ومن كان مسكنه وراء الميقات عند أبي حنيفة

rows.speaker: طاووس
rows.claim: Tawus takes the category to mean people of the non-sanctuary area.
rows.anchor: وأهل الحل عند طاوس

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik takes it to mean everyone except the people of Mecca.
rows.anchor: وغير أهل مكة عند مالك رضي الله تعالى عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For al-Shafii, “present” contrasts with traveler; for the other definitions, it means present or resident as opposed to absent.
rows.anchor: والحاضر على الوجه الأول ضد المسافر وعلى الوجوه الأخر بمعنى الشاهد الغير الغائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The presence of the family means the pilgrim’s own presence; family is used because a man usually lives where his family lives.
rows.anchor: والمراد من حضور الأهل حضور المحرم وعبر به لأن الغالب على الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masjid al-Haram can mean the mosque itself or the whole sanctuary; the latter is used in the Isra verse, and most leading scholars take it broadly here.
rows.anchor: وللمسجد الحرامإطلاقان أحدهما نفس المسجد والثاني الحرم كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Fear God” leaves its object unstated to include all commands and prohibitions, with Hajj especially included and thus connected to the surrounding discussion.
rows.anchor: في كل ما يأمركم به وينهاكم عنه كما يستفاد من ترك المفعول ويدخل فيه الحج دخولا أوليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The severe-punishment warning calls those who do not heed God to remember it and refrain from disobedience; naming God explicitly rather than by pronoun creates awe.
rows.anchor: لمن لم يتقه أي استحضروا ذلك لتمتنعوا عن العصيان وإظهار الأسم الجليل في موضع الإضمار لتربية المهابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Severe” is an adjective annexed to its nominative subject.
rows.anchor: وإضافة شديد من إضافة الصفة المشبهة إلى مرفوعها
